newsitem.title: USA: PRESS DIGEST - Wall Street Journal - Dec 20.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Wall Street Journal - Dec 20.

text.p: The following stories were reported in Friday's edition of The Wall Street Journal:
- Stocks and Bonds surged, spurred by data suggesting the economy may be slowing.
- The U.S. trade deficit narrowed in October.
- The FTC is raising serious antitrust questions about Staples proposed $3.3 billion acquisition of Office Depot.
- Norfolk southern raised its hostile bid for Conrail by about $500 million to $10.5 billion in cash, hours after CSX revised its own offer.
- GM again advised analysts to trim their profit estimates for the company's fourth quarter.
- Disney is completing plans to launch a cable network focused on educational programs for children.
- Royal Caribbean Cruises was charged by a federal grand jury with repeatedly dumping bilge water containing oil and falsifying records.
- The FAA threatened to suspend the commercial licenses of 26 pilots working for South Korea's Asiana Air.
- Short interest rose 3.1 percent on the Big Board in the latest month.
- Joseph Jett won a victory over Kidder when a panel rejected Kidder's monetary claims against its former government bond chief.
- Former Lazard Freres partner Mark Ferber was sentenced to 33 months in prison and fined $1 million over charges related to a municipal bond influence peddling scheme.
- Merck and Rhone-Poulenc said they plan to merge their animal health business.
- Big contact lens makers were sued by attorneys general from 22 states.
- Britain's top financial regulator suggested reforms at the London Metal Exchange in the wake of the $2.6 billion Sumitomo copper trading loss.
- Investors in Tokyo have been trading an unusually high volume of shares of Toyota Motor Corp in recent weeks.
